product: Windows event logs / Sysmon / Defender / DHCP (also on-prem AD via Security log)
CrowdStrike Falcon telemetry (not CS_ALERTS / CS_DETECTS: those are alerts)
Linux auditd / syslog / Sysmon for Linux
Microsoft 365 (management activity: Exchange / SharePoint / Entra / Purview DLP)
Entra ID (Azure AD) sign-in and audit
Firewall appliances: network traffic for every platform + the device's own events
Network sensors, firewalls, proxies, DNS: count for network inputs on every platform
Privileged access management: ATT&CK Enterprise has no platform for it, so its events count for no route
Databases: ATT&CK Enterprise has no database platform, so their events count for no route
Email security gateways: not the mailbox's own logs that MITRE's Office Suite analytics read; their alerts count under security-product detections when they carry ATT&CK ids
Security-product alert feeds: what a product detected, not telemetry about the systems; they never make a platform seen (alerts with ATT&CK ids count under product detections)
Collector health (BindPlane): about the log pipeline, not the monitored systems
Generic UDM events with no source log type: the platform can't be known
Solaris / AIX / HP-UX: ATT&CK Enterprise has no platform for these Unix systems
CrowdStrike Falcon alerts (rules on them watch hosts)
AWS GuardDuty findings (rules on them watch AWS)
